subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Cardio-oncology: Cardiotoxicity Patterns and Surveillance

steps.tx: Anthracycline cytotoxic therapy carries cumulative risk of irreversible cellular damage. **Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity** type **1** is cumulative, dose-dependent, and associated with permanent **myocardial ultrastructural** damage and myocyte loss. Binding of doxorubicin to topoisomerase II-beta triggers persistent double-strand DNA breaks and iron-dependent reactive oxygen species generation, producing myocyte vacuolization and progressive dilated cardiomyopathy.
steps.say: Anthracycline cytotoxic therapy carries cumulative risk of irreversible cellular damage. Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity type 1 is cumulative, dose-dependent, and associated with permanent myocardial ultrastructural damage and myocyte loss. Binding of doxorubicin to topoisomerase II-beta triggers DNA breaks and free radical generation, producing dilated cardiomyopathy.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species & DNA Strand Breaks

steps.tx: Catalytic topoisomerase inhibition provides targeted cardioprotection during necessary anthracycline administration. **Dexrazoxane** is an intracellular iron-chelating agent that prevents free radical generation, approved as a **cardioprotective agent** for cumulative **doxorubicin** doses exceeding **300** mg/m2. Administered intravenously immediately prior to doxorubicin infusion, dexrazoxane significantly reduces clinical heart failure without reducing antitumor response or overall survival.
steps.say: Catalytic topoisomerase inhibition provides targeted cardioprotection during necessary anthracycline administration. Dexrazoxane is an intracellular iron-chelating agent that prevents free radical generation, approved as a cardioprotective agent for cumulative doxorubicin doses exceeding 300 mg/m2. Administered prior to doxorubicin, it significantly reduces clinical heart failure.

left.title: Dexrazoxane Cardioprotection
points: Reduces clinical heart failure risk by >50%

right.title: Administration Protocol
points: Dosed at 10:1 ratio relative to doxorubicin dose
Does not impair chemotherapy response rates
Safe and approved in metastatic breast cancer

steps.tx: Targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 can impair cardiac contractile recovery. **Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity** type **2** is not dose-dependent, characteristically non-structural and reversible upon drug interruption and initiation of **ACE inhibitors** and beta-blockers. In contrast to anthracyclines, anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody cardiotoxicity does not cause myocyte death on endomyocardial biopsy, and patients frequently tolerate successful re-challenge following left ventricular ejection fraction normalization.
steps.say: Targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 can impair cardiac contractile recovery. Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity type 2 is not dose-dependent, characteristically non-structural and reversible upon drug interruption and initiation of ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers. Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity does not cause myocyte necrosis, permitting safe re-challenge after ejection fraction normalization.

left.title: Type 1 (Anthracyclines)
points: Poor ejection fraction recovery despite therapy

right.title: Type 2 (Trastuzumab)
points: Absence of myocyte necrosis on biopsy
High rate of LVEF recovery upon withholding
Responds well to ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers

steps.tx: Subclinical myocardial deformation imaging detects cardiotoxicity prior to ejection fraction decline. Echocardiographic **global longitudinal strain** GLS detects early **subclinical myocardial dysfunction**; a relative reduction greater than **15%** from baseline predicts subsequent left ventricular ejection fraction decline. Routine surveillance with speckle-tracking echocardiography allows early detection, triggering immediate initiation of cardioprotective neurohormonal therapies with enalapril and carvedilol.

Echocardiographic global longitudinal strain GLS detects early subclinical myocardial dysfunction; a relative reduction greater than 15% from baseline predicts subsequent left ventricular ejection fraction decline. nodes.label: Prompt Initiation of ACE Inhibitors & Beta-Blockers

steps.tx: The left view maps squeezing along the **heart walls** in a four chamber slice, while the dotted bullseye on the right averages **muscle shortening** segment by segment. A relative fall of more than **fifteen percent** from baseline flags **hidden pump injury** before ejection fraction drops. Catching this early wobble lets clinicians start protective heart drugs promptly and adjust cancer therapy before lasting damage sets in.
steps.say: Strain imaging tracks how much each heart segment shortens during contraction, summarised in the colour coded bullseye map. A relative reduction beyond fifteen percent from the starting value signals hidden pump injury even while ejection fraction still looks normal. That early warning triggers protective therapy with agents such as ACE blockers and beta blockers, plus closer cardiac surveillance during ongoing cancer treatment.

vis.alt: A four chamber strain view with a bullseye map shows reduced muscle shortening signalling early pump injury.

steps.tx: Immune checkpoint activation can precipitate fulminant lymphocytic myocarditis. Immune **checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis** is a fulminant, life-threatening complication with mortality approaching **50%**, requiring immediate high-dose intravenous **methylprednisolone** **1000** mg daily. Presenting early with troponin elevation and heart block, treatment requires immediate permanent immunotherapy cessation, telemetry admission, and consideration of secondary immunosuppression with abatacept.

rows: First 3 to 12 weeks of ICI therapy
Baseline and serial high-sensitivity troponin monitoring
IV methylprednisolone 1,000 mg daily for 3 days
Deploy secondary immunosuppression: abatacept or infliximab

steps.tx: Fluoropyrimidine antimetabolites exert acute coronary vasomotor toxicity independent of underlying plaque. **Fluoropyrimidines** 5-FU **fluorouracil** and **capecitabine** can trigger **coronary vasospasm** and myocardial ischemia, managed by immediate drug cessation, nitrates, and calcium channel blockers. Most commonly manifesting during 46-hour continuous infusional regimens, severe vasospasm can cause ventricular arrhythmias or cardiogenic shock, and drug re-challenge is generally contraindicated.

Severe vasospasm can cause shock during continuous infusional regimens, and re-challenge is generally contraindicated.

left.title: Fluoropyrimidine Vasospasm
points: Resting retrosternal chest tightness during infusion
Transient ST-segment elevation on continuous ECG
Driven by vascular endothelial nitric oxide depletion

steps.tx: Vascular endothelial growth factor pathway inhibition regularly provokes systemic vascular dysfunction. **VEGF inhibitors** **bevacizumab**, **sunitinib**, and **axitinib** frequently induce systemic **arterial hypertension** in up to **80%** of patients through endothelial nitric oxide reduction and capillary rarefaction. Prompt blood pressure monitoring and aggressive management with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers prevents target organ hypertensive complications.
steps.say: Vascular endothelial growth factor pathway inhibition regularly provokes systemic vascular dysfunction. VEGF inhibitors bevacizumab, sunitinib, and axitinib frequently induce systemic arterial hypertension in up to 80% of patients through endothelial nitric oxide reduction and capillary rarefaction. Prompt blood pressure monitoring and management with ACE inhibitors or calcium channel blockers prevents complications.

steps.tx: Serial electrocardiographic vigilance is essential for small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Baseline and serial **QTc interval** monitoring is mandatory for patients receiving targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors like **ribociclib**, **sunitinib**, or **vandetanib**, intervening when QTc exceeds **500** ms. Prolongation beyond 500 ms or an increase greater than 60 ms requires dose interruption, electrolyte correction of potassium and magnesium, and avoidance of QT-prolonging antiemetics.

rows: Interrupt if QTc > 500 ms; serial ECG on days 1 & 14
Keep QTc < 450 ms; regular serum K+ and Mg2+ checks
Correct electrolyte deficits prior to each cycle
Extremely high risk of ventricular arrhythmia
Maintain potassium > 4.0 mEq/L and magnesium > 2.0 mg/dL

steps.tx: **QTc prolongation** is a further cardio-oncology concern. Some tyrosine kinase inhibitors and antiemetic agents can lengthen the corrected QT interval, so a baseline **ECG** and serial tracings are sensible. Correcting abnormal blood chemistry and reviewing other QT-prolonging medicines lowers arrhythmic risk. Current European guidance favours a structured **risk assessment** that combines troponin, natriuretic peptides, strain imaging and multidisciplinary review.
steps.say: QTc prolongation is a further concern in cardio-oncology. Some tyrosine kinase inhibitors and antiemetic agents can lengthen the corrected QT interval, so a baseline electrocardiogram and repeated tracings are sensible. Correcting abnormal blood chemistry and reviewing other medicines that prolong the QT interval lowers the risk of arrhythmia. Current European guidance favours a structured risk assessment that combines troponin, natriuretic peptides, strain imaging and review by a multidisciplinary team.
